The Prevention Plan

After the catastrophic flood in 2001, the government asked the Japan International Cooperation Agency to help build a flood mitigation plan. Apart from an early warning system, JICA recommended three interventions to prevent all of Islamabad’s water from flowing to Rawalpindi.

Scroll to follow the plan ↓

JICA plan

The first was a community pond in F-9 Park. The pond would help check the flow of one of the tributaries and add an attraction to the park.

JICA plan

The second was building a dam on the Johd Kas, near the Golra village, next to E-11. This would help check flow to Bedarawali Kas, one of the Lai’s biggest tributaries.

JICA plan

The third was a diversion channel, that would take water from the tributaries eastwards to the Korang River directly.

JICA plan

JICA proposed three routes, along the Srinagar Highway, Khayaban-e-Johar and IJP Road. It recommended the second route as the most feasible.

But apart from the early warning system, the plan never came to fruition for multiple reasons.

CDA believed that it was not practical or feasible for several reasons.

Instead they came up with something less invasive.

CDA plan

Their first plan was to install 100 groundwater recharge wells across the H and I sectors. More wells are on the way.

CDA plan

Their second plan was to divert the stream around D-12 and E-11 to save it from flooding. This would help save the capital’s most flood-prone area immediately. The diversion is in the final stages of planning.

CDA plan

Then, they planned storage tanks at the foothills of the Margalla Hills. These tanks would store the rainwater before sewage has mixed in and help prevent overflows downstream.

CDA plan

But the most ambitious is CDA’s plan for rainwater harvesting, which has now been mandated in the city’s building codes.

CDA believes a third of the city’s rainfall volume can be harvested through rooftops.
